validated_results.title: Dietary isoflavones may protect against prostate cancer in Japanese men.
validated_results.reason: Original case-control study of Japanese men reporting odds ratios for prostate cancer risk in relation to dietary soy isoflavone intake, providing a target-specific estimate.

extraction.comparison_type: highest vs lowest category of isoflavone intake (>=89.9 mg/d vs <30.5 mg/d)

cases.excerpt: Two hundred patients and 200 age-matched controls (+/-5 y) were selected from 3 geographic areas of Japan. BMI, physical activity, occupation, family history of prostate cancer, and medical history were not associated with prostate cancer risk.

effect_size.excerpt: Isoflavones and their aglycones (genistein and daidzein) were significantly associated with decreased risk. The odds ratio for the highest category (> or = 89.9 mg/d) compared with the lowest category (<30.5 mg/d) of isoflavone intake was 0.42 (95% CI = 0.24-0.72) and the linear trend was significant (P < 0.01).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The odds ratio for the highest category (> or = 89.9 mg/d) compared with the lowest category (<30.5 mg/d) of isoflavone intake was 0.42 (95% CI = 0.24-0.72) and the linear trend was significant (P < 0.01).
